text: Market watchdogs plan dedicated capital market for start-ups, new derivatives in 2027

HÀ NỘI - Việt Nam is preparing to establish a specialised trading market for innovative start-ups and introduce index options in 2027, as part of broader efforts to diversify investment products, attract long-term capital and modernise its stock market infrastructure.

The plans were outlined by Phạm Thị Thùy Linh, head of the Securities Market Development Department at the State Securities Commission (SSC), during a discussion titled 'Capital Market 2027 - New Capital Flows, New Structures, New Investment Opportunities'.
Linh said Việt Nam needed to develop its capital market across three areas: expanding the supply of listed securities, diversifying investment products and strengthening its investor base.
Individual measures would not be sufficient to attract and retain long-term capital, she said.
One of the most notable initiatives is a proposal to establish a dedicated trading segment for innovative start-ups.
The SSC plans to submit the proposal to the Ministry of Finance and the Government for consideration, with a view to implementation in 2027, according to Linh.
Details of the proposed market, including its organisational structure, listing requirements and trading mechanism, have yet to be announced.
The initiative is intended to create a public capital-raising channel for innovative businesses seeking medium- and long-term funding.
The SSC is also working to improve the supply of high-quality securities through initial public offerings linked to stock exchange listings.
The existing regulatory framework has seen positive changes and brought opportunities for eligible foreign-invested enterprises to raise capital and list their shares publicly, according to SSC.
The range of investment products is also expected to expand.

Index options are scheduled for introduction in 2027, with additional guiding circulars expected to be issued later this year to establish the necessary legal framework for the risk-management instrument.

In addition, the regulator is working with the stock exchanges and the Vietnam Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation to study the development of a carbon credit market and specialised trading services for institutional investors.
These initiatives are being supported by amendments to the Securities Law, which formally introduce a controlled testing, or sandbox, mechanism.

Minister of Finance Ngô Văn Tuấn said the sandbox framework was designed to address the specific regulatory requirements of the securities sector, based on legislation governing science, technology and innovation.
The mechanism would allow organisations to test new technologies and business models within limited geographical and time boundaries under close supervision.
It would require safeguards covering asset segregation, data security and investor protection before successful models can be expanded more broadly.
CCP clearing system targets 2027 operation
Improving post-trade infrastructure is another priority, particularly as Việt Nam seeks to attract more foreign investment.
The SSC has been holding monthly discussions with international credit-rating agencies and investment institutions to address barriers to foreign participation.

Several technical obstacles have been tackled, including the introduction of a non-prefunding mechanism and arrangements allowing foreign investors to connect to the market through global securities firms.
Market-entry procedures have also been simplified.
Foreign investors can now complete the opening of a securities trading account within one day.
Meanwhile, the State Bank of Vietnam has removed the consular legalisation requirement that had applied to the opening of indirect investment capital accounts.
A key development is the planned introduction of a central counterparty (CCP) clearing mechanism, which is approaching the implementation stage.

Following the completion of the technical system and the Ministry of Finance's issuance of guiding regulations in September, the SSC is reviewing applications from securities companies and custodian banks for certificates to provide clearing services under the CCP mechanism.
The regulator is targeting the official operation of the system in 2027.
However, the SSC has also noted that foreign capital flows are cyclical and strongly influenced by fluctuations in global financial markets.
Developing domestic institutional investors is therefore a key priority for building a more stable source of market liquidity.

The planned expansion of listed products, introduction of new investment instruments and modernisation of post-trade infrastructure are being pursued alongside efforts to strengthen the domestic investor base.
These initiatives form part of Việt Nam's broader strategy to develop a deeper capital market and support its next phase of growth from 2027. - BIZHUB/VNS
